## Step 87 - the two entities a portal the player opens is, the colour its manager gives it, the twenty seconds it has, and the burst it leaves (built)

The visuals plan's step 7.4 (the remake's `out/parity/visuals/briefs/00_order.md` section 7, batch 7; its brief
`system_7.md` 7d-1 and G.3). Track B, on the `visuals-c` tree, after steps 81 (6.1), 82 (6.2), 83 (6.3), 84 (7.1),
85 (7.2) and 86 (7.3) - the merge renumbers. Game-only: the engine submodule stays at `4bfcf67` and no file under
`engine/` is touched. Changed: `game/data/{effects,placement}.json`, `game/sim/{Effects,Portals,Game}.{hpp,cpp}`,
`game/MagicPortalsLayer.{hpp,cpp}` and `tests/test_mp_{effects,statics,layer,play,launchers}.cpp`.
**A portal the player opens is no longer a white disc the port draws for it: it is the entity the original's script
adds, with the spiral and the iris the entity carries, the colour its manager gives it, the hover its callback gives
it, twenty seconds to live, and a burst where it dies.**

**BLOCKERS CHECKED.** 7.4's blockers are **6.3**, F2 and **R14**. 6.3 is step 83 (`d36abef`), committed in this
tree. **F2 exists** and is complete (`out/parity/footage/F2.md`, 1-3 at 16.3 fps): the row says it confirms dynamics
and does not measure them, and that is how it is used below. **R14, the unapplied 20,000 ms perish, is decided as
the original plays it** - the owner's standing ruling that every one of R1-R23 goes the way of the decode - so it is
applied here. Section **8.13 does not amend 7.4**, so section 7's row stands as written. Two other standing rulings
are used rather than decided: **R10**, the player at the z 4 the decode gives it (1.42 on the level's axis), which is
what a portal's decoded z of 0 is read against; and **R12**, the 720 selection, whose 720 / 256 = 2.8125 is the
factor `art.json depth` carries.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (the listing `out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce...`; the entities under
`reference/extracted/assets/entities/`).
- **`PortalManager::insertPortal`** (142281..142841) adds **two** entities for every portal a shot opens:
  #4-33 `AddEntity('portal_summon_effect.ent', vector3(pos, g_scale.scale(32)), 0, @out, '', getScale())`, then
  #47-71 `AddEntity('portal.ent', vector3(pos, 0f), 0f, @portal, 'portal.ent', getScale())`. The bubble is added
  FIRST, which is the order the two draw their random in.
- **`portal.ent` IS the portal.** `<Sprite>portal_halo.png</Sprite>` at blendMode 1 (added), applyLight 0, emissive
  (1, 1, 1), no `<Light>`; sys0 4 x `portal_spiral.png` a1 rep0, life 900 +- 450, size 70, growth -0.8, angleDir 1.3,
  `<StartPoint>` z 10; sys1 1 x `portal.png` a0 rep0, life 100, size 64, `<StartPoint>` z 10; and `<CustomData>`
  float `speed` 1, float `stride` 2, which are `linearMotion`'s.
- **`ETHCallback_portal`** (359141..359885) runs on it every frame, and it is four arms.
  - **#1-10 it hovers:** `linearMotion(thisEntity, vertical true, 0f, 0f)`, arguments pushed last-first (00_order
    8.0 rule 3; #3 `SetV1 v3, v1` is the 8-bit immediate 1). With the `.ent`'s speed 1 and stride 2 that is
    `y = y_opened + 2 cos(t)`, one radian a second, a 6.283 s period, from its lowest point.
  - **#12-86 it perishes:** uint `elapsedTime` is SET TO 0 on the first call (#22-37) and adds
    `getLastFrameElapsedTime()` on every later one (#38-53); past 20000 (#65, a strict compare) and with uint
    `dontPerish` zero (#67-79) it calls `killPortal`. **`dontPerish` is set by exactly one scene, and it is not a
    level**: `scenes/loading_screen.esc` carries `<Type>uint</Type><Name>dontPerish</Name><Value>1</Value>` in the
    `<CustomData>` of its own entity named `portal` - the same `portal.png` system, lifeTime 100, size 64, beside
    float `speed` 1 and `stride` 2 - so the loading screen's portal is the one portal in the game that stands for
    ever. **No level scene and none of the 190 `.ent` files names it**, and `insertPortal` never sets it on a portal
    a shot opens, so every portal the PLAYER opens perishes; `GetUInt` of a name that is not there is 0
    (`ETHEntity.cpp:865-870`), which is what those portals read. **This line said "never set" until the fix round
    below**: all 323 `.ent` and `.esc` files are UTF-16, so a plain grep over them finds nothing at all, and the
    census that produced it was one. Re-run with a BOM-driven reader it finds this one hit and no other; the two
    other `.esc`/`.ent` censuses of this batch (step 85's `explosion.ent`, step 82's ten `light_off` scenes) were
    made by parsers rather than greps and both reproduce exactly.
  - **#87-158 it fades:** `killTime` is READ (#99-101) before the block that WRITES it (#113-123), so the frame that
    notices the kill neither fades nor counts; from the next, `SetColor(GetColor() x 0.9)` every frame (#130-142).
  - **#159-185 it dies:** once `GetTime() - killTime` passes 400 (#157),
    `AddScaledEntity('portal_death.ent', GetPosition(), getScale())` and then `DeleteEntity`.
- **`killPortal`** (357278..357358) is `KillParticleSystem(0)` and `(1)`, which is `Kill(true)`
  (`ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:812-819`): no particle is renewed and each lives out the life it has. `ParticlesKilled(n)`
  returns that flag itself (`:821-828`), so it is true from the kill on and not when the pool is spent.
- **`PortalManager::update`** (138545..139692) is POP, THEN SIZE, THEN COLOUR, THEN POP, and the order is the whole
  of it. **#164-180** reads `portals[0].ParticlesKilled(0)` and, if it is set, calls `popFront` - ONE conditional
  (`#177 JLowZ -> 181`), no loop. **#181-188** then reads the size and compares it with the immediate 1.
  **Above one**: **#189-208 `portals[0]` = PORTAL_RED (1, 0.3, 0.4)** and **#209-228 `portals[1]` = PORTAL_BLUE
  (0.3, 0.4, 1)**, and only THEN, **#230-246**, a killed `portals[1]` is popped with `popBack` - again one
  conditional. **Exactly one** (#248-255): **#261-280 red** where `maxPortals` is 1, **#282-301 V3_ZERO**
  anywhere else - and that branch jumps to #302 WITHOUT popping, so a lone killed portal is coloured this frame and
  taken by the NEXT frame's front-pop. Zero: nothing at all, and #64-72 has already returned on an empty array.
  Nothing colours index 2 or beyond, and nothing recolours a portal it has popped. The globals are listing lines
  60476 and 60485. **`killAll` pops nothing** (147664..148016 #28-82: `killPortal` per entry and
  `decrementPortalCounter` for each that carried nothing), and it runs at **#105-106 of update**, before all of the
  above - so the clear button's pair is popped and coloured by the rest of that same update. **The port passes
  `budget` where the original reads `maxPortals`**, and `budget` is `min(maxPortals, 2)`: the two differ only above
  2, and there the original's answer for a lone portal is V3_ZERO either way, so every value the game can reach
  agrees.
- **Only the SPRITE reads that colour.** `SetColor` writes `m_v4Color` (`ETHEntity.cpp:493-498`); the sprite draws
  `min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color` (`ETHRenderEntity.cpp:112-117`); the particle pass draws
  `particle.color x ambient` and never reads it (`ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389`). 00_order 8.2 cites the same four
  call sites while ruling the STATIC portal's tint out of them. **So V3_ZERO on an added sprite is a halo that does
  not draw**, which is exactly what the original's own 1-3 still shows (`out/parity/smoke/nav/01`): a white spiral, a
  black core, and no glow.
- **The footage agrees.** F2 measures the hover at amplitude 1.95 and 1.89 u and omega 1.012 and 0.998 rad/s on the
  two portals of a 1-3 pair; it sees the summon bubble grow 382 u/s against the `.ent`'s 384; it records "no halo
  tint" on a lone portal and "A's halo turns pink on this same frame" that B opens; and it sees both ends killed by
  a teleport, `portal_death` about 0.45 s later, and the pair gone.

**WHAT CHANGED.**
- **`data/effects.json`** gains `portal_summon_effect`, `portal` and `portal_death` - three point-only rows, refused
  by `Effects::LoadRules` if either is given a direction - and **`placed_portal`**, the callback's own six numbers:
  the three colours, the 0.9 a frame, the 1/60 s of frame time it is taken over, and the 400 ms.
- **`data/placement.json`** gains `portal.perish_ms` 20000 and `portal.bob` (speed, stride, vertical, axis, start
  angle), both read by `Portals::LoadPlacement`, both with the instruction ranges above.
- **`sim/Effects`** gains those rows, `Summon`/`Portal`/`Death`, `ManagerColour` (the manager's #185-300 read in its
  own order) and `KillFade`.
- **`sim/Portals`.** `Placed` gains `basePx` - `linearMotion`'s `originalPos`, where the shot opened it - a
  `Motion::Linear` of its own, and `ageMs`. `Tick` runs the callback's first two arms over every placed portal
  before anything reads where one is: `Motion::Advance`, then `atPx = basePx + OffsetPx`, then `Centre`, which puts
  the entry circle back over the point. **ONE POINT AND NOT TWO** (00_order 8.15 R25's rule, here for a portal):
  `linearMotion` ends in `SetPosition` and `PortalManager::doTeleporting` reads that same `GetPositionXY`, so the
  circle a traveller enters by hovers with the picture. `sim/Motion` is step 69's, reused rather than copied;
  `Game::LoadData` reads `motions.json` once into `Data::motion` and hands it to the portals' rules.
- **AND `State` GAINS `nextPortalId`, WHICH IS NOT THE COUNT OF PORTALS USED.** The original's manager holds
  ETHEntity HANDLES, and a handle is never handed out twice; `portalsUsed` is the GOLDEN SCORE's count, and
  `killAll(true)` gives it back for every portal that carried nothing (`decrementPortalCounter`, killAll #47-72).
  Naming a portal by that refundable count - which is what `TryPlace` did until the fix round below - let the
  clear-portals button hand a new portal the id of one whose entity was still inside its 400 ms, and the layer's
  id-keyed drawing then gave the new portal the dying one's colour, withheld its own two entities, and burst it.
  `nextPortalId` is handed out once and never given back, so an id is a portal's for the level's life.
- **`MagicPortalsLayer::syncPlacedPortals`**, per FRAME beside `updateEffects`, and it is `PortalManager::update`'s
  own four steps in its own order: a new id adds the bubble and then `portal.ent` through the effects runtime; an id
  that has left the simulation's list has its two systems killed; **the manager's array** - the drawn portals it has
  not popped, which is NOT the list of portals in play - has a killed front popped, then what is left coloured by
  its size, then a killed `portals[1]` popped; and from the frame after a kill the colour falls and the 400 ms runs
  out into `portal_death.ent` and the end of the entity. `DrawnPortal` carries `popped` for exactly that array.
  `m_portalQuads` - the port's own white halo quad - is gone with it.
- **`EffectSpawn` gains `pictureSlot` and `colour`, and `Effect` a `colour`.** The between-slot table names a portal
  the player opened in its own right (00_order K13), so its picture keeps `Slot::PlacedPortal` where every other
  added entity takes `Slot::Effect`; the table itself is untouched, and its halo and systems keep their own classes.
  The colour is written onto the picture's quad in `updateEffects` and not in `syncLighting`, because an effect is
  added and faded on the frame: a tint that waited for the next tick would draw a new portal white for a frame and a
  dying one at its old brightness.
- **The capture harness learns the tap it always meant.** `readInput` read the pointer through `Input` directly for
  the shot, so a scheduled `--tap` - which owns the pointer through `touchThisTick` - could close a popup and press a
  help block but could never fire a portal, and 7.4's gate could not be run at all. `readInput` now reads the tick's
  touch ONCE, hands it to `helpBlockInput` and fires the shot from it, and `ScreenToLevelPx` splits into
  `ViewportToLevelPx` so a touch that has no cursor can be mapped. **For a REAL pointer it changes nothing** - the
  touch it now reads carries the same `pointerOverGame` and `TickWasPressed(kTap)` it read before - and for a
  scheduled tap it changes one thing: a tap that used to do nothing now fires. The 128-level sweep takes no tap at
  all, and the only tap in this step's own captures besides the shots is the popup close, which the popup consumes
  before `readInput` reaches the shot. 10.1's gates need the same seam.
- **`Slot`, `SlotRow` and `kSlotTable` moved up the header** above the effects block, unchanged, so that
  `EffectSpawn` can name a class. No line of the table itself changed.

**THE DEPTH THIS MOVES, and it is one level.** A placed portal used to be drawn at `slotAt(m_playerSlot, ...)` -
the player's own slot - and is now drawn at `slotAfter(0, ...)`, which is the decoded z 0 of `portal.ent`. The two
are the same wherever no node stands between 0 and the player's 1.42, which is every level but level22a
(`art.json depth`: one node at eth_z 1 in the whole game). No capture here shows level22a with a portal on it, and
the change is written down rather than measured.

- **The core's `<= 25` sits inside the method noise of the reference it came from.** Read on the ORIGINAL's still,

1. **A REUSED ID (high, and a real defect).** `TryPlace` named a portal `portalsUsed`, and `KillAll(true)` - the

   the id of one whose entity was still inside its 400 ms fade, and the layer's id-keyed list then did three wrong
   things at once: the `known` check suppressed the new portal's summon bubble and `portal.ent` entirely, the
   re-bind handed the DYING entry the live portal's point, and 400 ms later that entry freed the picture and burst
   `portal_death.ent` on a portal that was alive. **The verifier's own two-line guard was not enough** and the fix
   is the sim's, not the layer's: `effectOwnerPoint` looks an effect's owner up by id over `m_portalDraws` and
   returns the FIRST match, so with a frozen dying entry ahead of a live one sharing its id, the new portal's own
   picture would still have followed the dead one's point. `Portals::State::nextPortalId` splits the two things the
   original keeps apart - the refundable SCORE counter and the never-reused entity HANDLE - and the layer keeps a
   `!drawn.killed` guard on its identity search anyway, so its drawing is right on its own terms. Pinned by
   `test_mp_layer`'s new clear-button case, which drives the real control (the suite can press it; a scheduled
   `--tap` still cannot, because `readInput` takes `under = devTap ? nullptr : ...`).

What it costs is that the effects' stream has two consumers whose ORDER matters, and the order is `OnUpdate`'s:

**THE SWEEP, LEVEL BY LEVEL** (`8.2/after/sweep`, each png's md5 matching its log line; `8.2/compare_sweep.py`
-> `compare_sweep.json`; channel deltas `channel_deltas.json`; crops in `8.2/crops/`). THE DISCRIMINATING HALF:
the 110 levels whose carriers state exactly their `.ent`'s systems, or differ from it only in `StartPoint.z`
(which the port reads but draws nothing with until 8.4) - 1-01 and 1-15 with their static portals, and every
shock and fire diamond level - are **110 of 110 byte-identical**, so on every carrier of those levels the sidecar
loads what the `.ent` loaded. What decides how far a change reaches: every placed emitter draws from the one
placement stream, `m_particleRandom`, when its pool is made and whenever a particle is reborn (`Particles::Step`),
in `m_sprites`' order every frame, and a system with no spread draws nothing (`particleRandom` returns the bound
without a draw). A carrier whose new systems have spreads moves every emitter that draws after it, in that frame
and every later one; a carrier whose change draws the same numbers moves only itself. **This is not K8's case**:
K8 keeps the draws that are NOT placements (effects, eyes, aura) off this stream, and this is no effect step -
what moved is the level's own placed systems, whose draws are the placement stream by design.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **The fallback is gone** (`game/MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:766`). A drawn sprite with an empty `particles` is skipped;
  one with a path draws that sidecar's systems exactly as step 89 built it (the same `Load`, `Scale`, `MakePool`
  on `m_particleRandom`, in `m_sprites`' order), and a sidecar that will not load, or holds none, is still logged
  and skipped. The node -> entity-name map that only the fallback used is removed: `particles` comes only from the
  lighting read's `Look`, which holds only the level's entity nodes, so the map's filter kept exactly the sprites
  that can carry a path. The "particle system not drawn" warning now names the node and its sidecar. What the
  script adds is untouched and still reads `original/entities/<name>`: `addEntityEmitters` and the effects
  runtime's `Art::LoadEnt`.
- **Step 89's unlit-level question, ruled: such a level draws no placed particle system.** The key has one reader,
  `Lighting::Read`, and a level whose lighting read is refused has no `Look`, so it now loses its placements'
  particles with its lighting - a fault state, not a play mode, and none ships (`test_mp_lighting`: 128 of 128
  read). The warning says what it costs: "`<level>` drawn unlit, and without its placements' particle systems:
  ..." (`:443`). The alternative - a second reader of `eth_particles` for the unlit case - is the two-parser
  arrangement step 89 declined.
- **The reader refuses `eth_particles` on a node that draws no sprite** (`game/sim/Lighting.cpp:307`): "eth_particles
  on a node that draws no sprite, whose particles the port does not draw". The other half of step 89's latent row,
  which step 90 answered on the converter's side only. `buildEmitters` walks the level's sprites, so on a
  light-only node the key would be read and never drawn - a skip, against the reader's own "refused, never
  skipped". A PORT limit, not the engine's (`ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:106` loads a spriteless entity's systems); none
  ships. `Lighting.hpp`'s vocabulary now says "(only on a node that draws a sprite)".
- **Comments that counted the fallback, corrected**: `Particles.hpp` (`Drawable`) and `syncLighting`'s header said
  the levels place 889 systems (879 added, 10 mixed) - what the `.ent` files held; the levels place 897 (887 / 10).
  The `Look::particles`, `DrawnSprite::particles`, `buildEmitters` and vocabulary comments no longer say the `.ent`

The visuals plan's step 8.4 (the remake's `out/parity/visuals/briefs/00_order.md` section 7, batch 8; its brief

for 8.4, so section 7's row stands: "`test_mp_layer`: `blue_light`'s system after sprites with z <= 24; sweep

**THE OWNER'S STANDING RULINGS.** None of R1-R25 names this step. Two are used rather than decided, each as the
owner's standing ruling: **R10**, the player at the z 4 its constructor gives it, 4 / 2.8125 = 1.42 on the level's

**THE RUN'S PREMISE, CORRECTED: A `<StartPoint>` z IS NOT A BARE LITERAL.** This run's instruction for 8.4, and
step 86's hand-off to "the K13 owner", read a system's `<StartPoint>` z as the same kind of raw literal as a z the
script writes into a `vector3`, to be divided by R12's 2.8125. The engine source says otherwise, and where the two
disagree the engine source is the spec (CLAUDE.md):
- `ETHParticleSystem::Scale` multiplies the whole `startPoint` vector3, z included, with the sizes
  (`Particles/ETHParticleSystem.cpp:27-33`); the manager applies it when it is made (`ETHParticleManager.cpp:90`) at
  the entity's own mean scale (`Entity/ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:316-319`), and a later `ETHEntity::Scale(float)` scales
  every system again (`Entity/ETHEntity.cpp:591-599` -> `ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:512-518` ->
  `ETHParticleManager.cpp:444-446`).
- **A placement.** `LoadScene` scales by the engine's global factor (`Script/ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:603`), which
  this game never sets: it defaults to 1 (`Util/ETHGlobalScaleManager.cpp:27`), and the listing has no
  `SetFixedHeight` or `SetScaleFactor` call. The script's `SGlobalScale::scaleEntities` (6838..7228) then calls
  `scaleEntity` (6072..6337) on every entity: #30-36 `Scale(getScale() x individualScale)`, #38-53
  `SetPosition(GetPosition() x getScale())`. The start point's z and the position's z are scaled by the same factor,
  so on the level's axis the start point's z is the file's number (times a `scale` custom datum, which none of the 15
  carriers has; `scalable` 0 would skip an entity, and no scene or `.ent` sets it).
- **A script's `AddEntity`.** The entity is made at `Scale() x globalScale` (`ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:131-158`,
  `ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:56-65`), and every call site the port draws passes `g_scale.getScale()` or `g_scale.scale(k)`:
  `appearEffect` 357060..357278 #2-6 and #26, `vanishEffect`, `insertPortal`, `addFireball`, `explode`
  342023..342895 #1-23, the character's constructor, `ETHCallback_portal`, `ETHCallback_fireball`. So an effect's
  start point z is on the level's axis at the effect's own scale, which `Particles::Scaled` already gives it in
  `SpawnEffect`. **The effects runtime needs no change**: the appear ring's flash at 0.711 + 10, the eyes' 2 and the
  fireball's 4 x its scale stand as steps 84-86 drew them. Only its two comments, which called the z a raw literal,
  are corrected (`effectAdd`'s and `SpawnEffect`'s). None of the eleven effect `.ent`s the port spawns is
  `ET_VERTICAL`, so the shift below never reaches them.
- Screen projection is no concern either: `DrawParticleSystem` draws each particle at `pos + zAxisDirection x
  startPoint.z` (`ETHParticleManager.cpp:392`, `Util/ETHASUtil.cpp:123-126`), but all 133 of the game's `.esc` files
  set `<ZAxisDirection x="0" y="0" />`, so the z moves nothing on the screen.
- Written into `docs/ethanon-formats.md` as 7.4a, with the citations.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **`buildEmitters`** (`game/MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:812-840`): each emitter now carries `depth` = its owner's `eth_z`
  (`DrawnSprite::lookZ`) + its system's `startPointZ` (at the entity's scale, `Particles::Scale`) and `lifted` = that
  z is not 0. A system at 0 - 872 of the 897 - is placed exactly as before, `systemZ(drawn.z, Slot::Systems, ...)`,
  in its owner's slot. A lifted one is placed at `systemZ(slotAfter(depth, Slot::Picture), Slot::LiftedSystems,
  ...)`: after every picture whose `z_index` is at or below the depth, after the player where 1.42 is at or below
  it (`slotAfter`'s own rule), before every picture above it. The depth is not rounded: `slotAfter` compares it with
  each picture's `z_index` as it already compares the wall ghost's unrounded depth, and on the 15 carriers it is a
  whole number anyway. **The pools, their order and their stream are untouched**: the emitters are made in the same
  order from the same systems on `m_particleRandom`, and only a z moves (K8 as step 85 reads it).
- **One new row, `Slot::LiftedSystems`** ("lifted particle systems", fraction -1/2, spreading;
  `game/MagicPortalsLayer.hpp`), between `Slot::Effect` and `Slot::PlacedPortal`, so the table stays in drawing
  order. Spreading from -1/2 puts a lifted system in (-1/2, -1/4) of the slot of the first thing drawn above its
  depth - the one quarter of a gap no other row stands on or spreads over (the eleven other -1/2 rows stand exactly
  at -1/2, the three -1/4 rows at -1/4, and `EffectSystems` spreads over (-1/4, 0)) - so it ties with nothing. **K13
  is met**: a new between-slot depth is a row of the table, no lambda, and the order is pinned in `test_mp_layer`.
  The row's cost is the table's own limit, now written beside it: in a gap two classes share, the original orders
  them by depth and the table by class, so the picture of an effect deeper than a lifted system but in its gap
  still draws behind it, and the halo and systems of an effect shallower than it still draw in front of it.
- **`EmitterReport`** gains `depth` and `lifted`; **`PictureReports()`** is new - each level picture's node,
  `z_index`, `eth_z` and slot z, in drawing order - for the suite to measure a lifted system against.
- **`test_mp_layer`**:
  - `AStartPointLiftsAPlacementsSystems` (new, `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp:3291`): over the 128 levels, the carriers
    whose sidecar holds a start point z other than 0 are exactly the 15 listed, with their `eth_z`, their z and
    their system count, 25 of 897 systems; then on each of the 15 levels, each of the carrier's systems is `lifted`
    at its depth, in front of every picture at or below it and of the player where 1.42 is at or below it, behind
    every picture above it, a quarter to a half of a slot before the next thing drawn (picture or player), with its
    pool as its sidecar states it (4; 18 and 2); every other system on the level keeps its owner's slot; and the
    plan's own words on level4 (1-05's orb after every picture with `z_index` <= 24) and a picture at exactly the
    depth staying behind (level21c's `button_1723` at -6).
  - `TheBetweenSlotTableSaysWhereEachClassStands`: the new row's fraction and place (after `Effect`, before
    `PlacedPortal`), eleven NON-spreading rows at -1/2 (the tie the table states is unchanged) and three spreading
    rows, not two.
  - **The six dangling reads, fixed as this suite's first change** (backlog, step 91): each
    `ReportOf(layer.EmitterReports(), ...)` now holds the reports in a local, and a **deleted** overload of
    `ReportOf` for a temporary vector (`:2721-2726`) makes a seventh a compile error. The suite compiled with it, so

- No data file changes: the rule has no tunable number. The vertical shift's 10, when it is built, is the engine's

**NOT BUILT: THE VERTICAL SHIFT.** Ethanon adds `_ETH_PARTICLE_DEPTH_SHIFT` (`Particles/ETHParticleManager.h:30`,
10.0 raw world units, 10 / 2.8125 = 3.556 on the level's axis) to the depth of an `ET_VERTICAL` owner's pieces
(`ETHParticleManager.cpp:332-335`, through `ETHEntityProperties::ResolveDepthSortingMode`,

told a placement's type** - the converter writes none - and adding it is a K10 pair (the reader accepts a key, then

original draws the sparkles over and the port does not. The lift built here moves the sparkles toward the
original's depth and never past it (deviation 2).

## Step 93 - the scale a level's sprite is drawn at, read before the converter writes it: its units and its offset times it, its lightmap checked before it (built)

The visuals plan's step 9.1 (the remake's `out/parity/visuals/briefs/00_order.md` section 7, batch 9, "reader
first"; its brief `systems_9_10.md` 9a (4) "SE-game" and 9a (5); conflicts K9 and K10). Track A, on MPR `main` in
`build/`, after step 92 (`bd44717`). Game-only: the engine submodule stays at `4bfcf67` and no file under `engine/`
is touched; the converter and the converted levels are untouched (`out/levels`, `out/assets`, `out/data` and
`out/snap_pre8` are not written). Changed: `game/sim/Tscn.{hpp,cpp}`, `game/sim/Sprites.{hpp,cpp}`,
`game/sim/Lighting.{hpp,cpp}`, `game/sim/Particles.hpp` (comments), `game/MagicPortalsLayer.cpp` (one rule in
`buildEmitters`), `tests/test_mp_tscn.cpp`, `tests/test_mp_sprites.cpp`, `tests/test_mp_lighting.cpp`,
`tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`, `docs/ethanon-formats.md` (the lightmap's bake size) and the backlog. **The level reader
now takes `scale = Vector2(sx, sy)` on a Sprite2D - the entity's `<Scale>`, which 9.2's converter is to write on the
33 placements that state one - and refuses it anywhere else and in any form but two numbers above 0.
`Sprites::Find` draws the sprite at its whole units times that scale, with its offset times it (K9's combined
rule: the tier's density on the texels, then the truncation, then the scale; never the density on the offset);
`Lighting::Read` still checks a lightmap against the units before the scale; and a placement's own particle
systems are made at the mean of its scale, as the engine makes them. No converted level carries the key yet, so
every sprite's scale is 1 and every product is exact: the 128-level f420 sweep is 128 of 128 byte-identical to
step 92's. Gameplay: none - no body, collider or sensor reads the sprite's scale; the 31 barrel bodies and the 2-22
stone change only when 9.2 bakes the scale into their colliders (R9).**

**BLOCKERS CHECKED.** 9.1's two blockers are met: **2.2 (K9)** is step 66 (`c404615`), which made `Find` resolve
the tier and size a sprite in whole units, and **8.3 (K10 pins)** is step 91 (`e71b697`), which pinned the counts
batch 8 moves; both are committed. Section 8.13 has no row for 9.1, so section 7's row stands: "`test_mp_tscn`
(`:120` replaced: scale accepted, zero or negative refused); 128 levels byte-identical", with the step's title
("`Find` applies K9's rule; the lightmap check stays on units") and the backlog's owed item - step 81's **latent K7
fixture**, "a placement with a scale other than 1 that owns a light, its halo pinned at `eth_halo_size`, not
scaled" - measured as gates too. **K10** is this step's half: the reader must accept the key, and be COMMITTED,
before 9.2's converter writes it. Step 89 found K10's "an unknown key fails the whole level" true for a node key
like this one (not for a `metadata/` key): before this step a Sprite2D `scale` failed `Tscn::Parse`, and with it
`Game::LoadData`. The baseline is step 92's after, `8.4/after/sweep`: its 128 PNGs match the md5s its
`capture.txt` logged (128 of 128, checked for power-loss damage before use), and `build/` held `d2504b6d`, the
binary 8.4's independent check captured it on, so no fresh "before" was needed and that binary was not launched.

**THE OWNER'S STANDING RULINGS.** **R13** (route B: the port resolves the tier, the level names the 1x file), as
the owner's standing ruling: it is why the scale arrives on its own and multiplies the resolved units, never
composed with a tier's 0.5 as plan_port's route A would have had it. **R9** (the `<Scale>` bodies, as the
original) is 9.2's and 9.3's to apply: this step changes no body. **R12** is not used: no depth moves. **R24 and
R25 (step 76) remain the owner's to rule**; this step neither applies nor withdraws them.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **`Tscn::Parse`** (`game/sim/Tscn.cpp:28-39`, `:427-435`): `scale` joins the node keys. On a node that is not a
  Sprite2D it is refused naming the line ("property 'scale' on a Node2D: only a Sprite2D's is in the subset") -
  the converter writes it on the Sprite2D alone and bakes it into the colliders instead (9a (4)), and on any other
  node it would scale something `LevelBuilder` builds unscaled. On a Sprite2D it must be a Vector2 of two numbers
  above 0 ("scale: a Sprite2D's scale is a Vector2 of two numbers above 0"): Godot would draw a negative one
  mirrored, and the 33 placements that state a `<Scale>` state 0.8 to 2 (`9.1/census/types91.py`, below). A
  scale of exactly 1 is accepted. `Tscn.hpp`'s subset list names it, "read before the converter writes it".
- **`Sprites::Find`** (`game/sim/Sprites.cpp:219-238`): `Sprite::scale` (new, `Sprites.hpp:61`) is the Sprite2D's
  scale, 1 where it states none; `sizePx = Tiers::Units(texels, density) x scale` and `offsetPx = offset x
  scale`, so `CentrePx`, the body branch of `syncSprites` and every picture placed from them take it. `texels`,
  `density` and the tier are untouched. It says so again, naming the line, for a scene built some other way than
  `Parse`. That is Ethanon's own rule: the frame times the scale (`ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize`,
  `ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-683`) about the pivot times the scale (`ETHEntity::ComputeAbsoluteOrigin`,
  `ETHEntity.cpp:296`), which is also Godot's for a Sprite2D's `scale` and `offset` - so the converter keeps writing
  `offset = -pivot` unscaled (9a (4)). `Sprites.hpp`'s header, which said "no scale is ever written", is corrected.
- **`Lighting::Read`** (`game/sim/Lighting.cpp:199-207`, `:319-336`): the lightmap is checked against
  `Tiers::Units(texels, density)` - the units BEFORE the scale - rather than against `sizePx`; the refusal now says
  "units". K9 required it and the engine confirms it: `ETHLightmapGen` bakes a lightmap on a render target of the
  sprite's bitmap size (`ETHLightmapGen.cpp:57`) with the entity's scale set to 1, each light's position and
  range divided by it (`:117-120`), and draws it over the scaled picture. Written into `docs/ethanon-formats.md`
  beside the lightmap copy rules. No shipped placement has both a `<Scale>` and a lightmap (census).
- **`buildEmitters`** (`game/MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:782-792`): a placement's own systems are scaled, in ONE
  `Particles::Scale` call, by `drawn.scale x (sx + sy) / 2` - the mean of its `<Scale>`, which the engine makes the
  entity's particle managers at (`ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:316-319`, `ETHParticleManager.cpp:90`), times what its script
  scales it by after (a static portal's 0.8, as before). One call, not two, so a static portal's systems are scaled
  by exactly the number they were (x 1.0 is exact). Its light and halo are NOT scaled: the converter writes
  `<Scale>` into them already, and a level placement passes owner scale 1 (K7, `syncLights`), unchanged. None of
  the 840 carriers states a `<Scale>` (census), so this moves nothing on a shipped level; it makes step 92's
  comment "the file's number at the entity's own scale - which Particles::Scale has applied above" true for a
  scaled carrier.
- **Carry-in from step 92: `sim/Particles.hpp`'s stale `startPointZ` comment** ("not yet drawn with") now says what
  steps 83-86 and 92 built; the `Scale` comment says how a placement's `<Scale>` enters.

**THE CENSUS** (`9.1/census/types91.py` -> `types91.json`, read-only over the 128 levels' `.esc` bodies): 4,065
placements; **33 with a `<Scale>` other than 1** - `barrel_bomb.ent` 1.3 x 29 and `barrel_bomb` 1.3 x 2, `eclipse.ent`
2.0 x 1, `rolling_stone` 0.8 x 1 - all type 0, **none with a light, a halo, a particle system or a lightmap**
(systems_9_10's census again); and by entity type, **4,055 of type 0 and 10 of type 2** (the ten `light_off`
torches), no other.

**NOT TAKEN: THE ENTITY-TYPE PAIR (step 92's carry-in).** Step 92 left the unlit torches' vertical particle shift
(`_ETH_PARTICLE_DEPTH_SHIFT` 10, 3.556 on the level's axis) for a reader-then-converter pair carrying the entity's
type, to be taken here and in 9.2 if it fitted cleanly. It does not. `ET_VERTICAL` is not one depth rule but six
(`docs/ethanon-formats.md` 5.3 and its lighting block): the particle shift (`ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:98-102`),
the draw hash's y term (`:132-134`), the halo drawn a sprite's height deeper (`:80`), no rotation
(`ETHRenderEntity.cpp:105`, `ETHEntity.cpp:621-624`), the centre-bottom origin (`ETHEntity.cpp:38-39`, already
written into the offset by the converter's `_vertical_offset`) and the vertical light and ambient shaders
(`ETHShaderManager.cpp:110`, `ETHPixelLightDiffuseSpecular.cpp:62`, `ETHVertexLightDiffuse.cpp:57`). All ten torches
apply light (`eth_apply_light "1"` and `eth_normal` on all ten nodes in `out/levels`). A key the lighting reader accepted for the
shift alone would be a lighting input it knowingly skips - the vertical shaders on all ten - against its own
"refused, never skipped"; refusing it on a lit node would refuse every torch level. Nothing was built for it; the
backlog row stays open with this finding.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **`tscn.py` `write_scene`**: `scale = Vector2(sx, sy)` on the Sprite2D, after its `offset`, only where `<Scale>` is
  not (1, 1); the offset stays `-pivotAdjust` (and `_vertical_offset`'s half height) unscaled, as step 93's reader
  expects. A `<Scale>` with a component not above 0 skips the instance with a report line (the port's reader refuses
  it, and the whole level with it); none ships. A joint's `joint_anchor_x/y` take `sx`/`sy`; its angles and motor
  do not. `trigger_size`/`trigger_offset` stay unscaled (the script's view). The `eth_*` lighting keys and the particle
  sidecars are written exactly as before: the converter already scales the light and halo per consumer and the port
  does not scale them again (K7); the port makes a placement's systems at the mean of the scale (step 93).
- **`tscn.py` `_collider_lines`**: the collision box's size and position times the scale per axis before any branch,
  so the box, the shape's `position`, the polygon and the circle's `(sx * w + sy * h) / 4` all come out scaled; a
  compound's fixtures (resolved by `entity._parse_compound` against the unscaled box) are multiplied through - offsets
  and box extents per axis, a circle's radius by `sx`. The body node never carries a scale.
- **`__main__.py`**: the report adds "scaled sprites: N; colliders with the scale baked in: M".
- **`tests/test_scale.py`, 11 tests on a hand-written scene**: the plan's fixture (a 1.3 barrel on a 22 x 29 box ->

  `lookZ`: 2 / 2.8125 for a marker's minion, the escort's for a summoned one); `cameraCornerPx` (the follow keeps the
  view's centre; Ethanon's camera is its top-left); `EffectReport::systemImage` for the suites.

**THE MULTIPLY, AND WHY IT IS EXACT HERE.** A black texel at an alpha of 255 - g through the engine's ordinary mix gives
`0 x a + d x (1 - a) = d x g / 255`, which is `GL_ZERO, GL_SRC_COLOR` over a grey texel and a white colour (E6:
`blackexplosion.png` and `black_portal_particle.png` are grey to the last texel; all four `alphaMode 4` systems the
original ships are white at both ends - `test_mp_sprites` checks both on the files). The colour's alpha must not weight
it again, which is K12's rule: blood lerps 0.2 -> 1, and a kept 0.2 would draw the blackest texel over 200 at 160. It
holds on a real frame because the port renders with `SceneEncoding::DisplayEncoded` (`MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:152`): the
float target holds display values and blends in display space, as the original's fixed-point target did; the engine's
default linear path would multiply in linear light and miss by tens of levels. The unit is measured on the engine's
blend formula at 8 bits, not on a frame: the port's output is quantised to RGB565 (`lighting.json`
`framebuffer_rgb565`), whose steps of 8 and 4 levels no captured pixel can resolve to +-1. The loading screen's black
halo is unchanged: the generalised function writes `entities_black_halo_multiply.png` byte-identical to the old
`black_halo_multiply.png` (md5 `3c0dd4e3`).

**K13** needs no new row: the four are effects, and take `Slot::Effect`, `Slot::EffectHalo` and `Slot::EffectSystems`
as step 83 left them; `TheBetweenSlotTableSaysWhereEachClassStands` is unchanged and green. **K8**: all four draw from
`m_effectRandom` through `SpawnEffect`, so the placement stream is untouched - `AnEffectMovesNoParticleOfTheLevels`
(step 83's check: a level's own emitters report the same values with an effect added) is green - and on a level where
one of them fires, every later effect's spread moves against a run where it does not, the reading step 85 recorded.

- **The door-flame pixels** (deviation 9; 8 on 3-09, 9 on 2-12, inside the final door's own additive flame): **every one differs by
  exactly one RGB565 level in exactly one channel** (5-bit R or B by 8, 6-bit G by 4). The mechanism is INFERRED from
  the code, not measured: a level emitter destroys a particle's quad when the particle is not drawn and makes a new
  one when it is (`stepEmitter`, `MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:983-1017`); the registry keeps components packed, and a removal
  moves the last one into the hole; and the transparent sort breaks a tie at equal depth by gather order
  (`RenderSystem::SortTransparentDraws`, engine `src/core/RenderSystem.cpp:158-176`). So effect quads coming and going
  reorder the flame's equal-depth additive quads, and a different summation order rounds differently in the float
  target. The flame's own particles do not move: that is K8's placement-stream check above. The merge of step 88
  recorded the same class on 4-14 (15 RGB565-step pixels where the door glow meets effect quads).

**THE OWNER'S STANDING RULINGS.** **R16 is applied** as the owner's standing ruling (in favour of what the original
does). **R10** (the character at z 4) and **R12** (720 / 256 = 2.8125) are used, not decided: a marker's minion stands at

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (the listing `out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce...`; the entities under
`reference/extracted/assets/entities/`).
- **The spawn.** `ETHCallback_minion_spawn` (426511..426876) #31-51 hands the marker's `GetString('entityName')` to
  `spawnMinion` (426876..427194), whose #1-23 replace an empty name with `'minion.ent'` and #25-39 `AddEntity(entityName,
  vector3(GetPositionXY(), 2), 0 (#32), out, alternativeName, getScale() (#25-29))`. The chapter-3 boss's rage arm hands
  it the literal `'minion.ent'` (`ETHCallback_ghost` ins 1137). Of the 62 markers in the 128 levels only level31b's
  `minion_spawn_908` names an entity (`test_mp_minions`' census, below).
- **The two files.** `ghost_minion.ent` states `minion.ent`'s body to the attribute: `<Entity>` shape 4, sensor 0, bullet
  0, fixedRotation 1, static 0, friction 0, density 0.5, restitution 0, gravityScale 1; the same `<Collision>` (at (0, 0,
  0), 14 x 36 x 1, the same two-circle `<Compound>`, CDATA-wrapped in one file and not the other); the same custom data,
  breakable, burnable and teleportable 1. What differs: `EmissiveColor` (0, 0, 0), `startFrame` 4, and one
  `<ParticleSystem>`: 24 `black_portal_particle.png`, not all at once, `alphaMode` 4, repeat 0, life 550 (rand 200), size
  18 shrinking 0.6, `<Direction>` (0, -0.8) spread (0.3, 0.3), `<StartPoint>` (0, -8, **-2**), `<RandStartPoint>` (0,
  24), `Color0` = `Color1` = (1, 1, 1, 1). `black_portal_particle.png` is 64 x 64 RGB, r = g = b at every texel, 0 to
  255 (E6).
- **The callbacks.** `ETHCallback_ghost_minion` (451487..451999): #8-18 `SetColor(V3_ZERO)` every frame; #25
  `ETHCallback_minion` - the same patrol, rows and holds; #27-33 `LoadSprite('entities/ghost.png')`; and #35-104, once
  `!IsAlive()`, `AddEntity('ghost.ent', currentPos + vector3(0, 0, scale(-1)), 0, out, '', scale(0.3))`,
  `playGhostAppearSound`, `DeleteEntity(SeekEntity(1430))` - R4, 12.2's. Most minion code does not tell the two apart:
  `isMinion` (437789..437964, what a killer floor asks) accepts both, `CharacterChooser::choose` (a key's carrier) accepts
  both, `MinionChooser::choose` (a shock diamond's prey) is `isMinion`, and the sight's ignore list names both
  (`ETHCallback_minion` #905). **Two places do tell them apart, by the entity's name** (corrected after the independent
  check; the first record said none did). The engine binds a body's contact callbacks by its entity's own name,
  `'ETHBeginContactCallback_' + RemoveExtension(GetEntityName())` (`ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:59`, `:66-70`), and
  the listing has `ETHBeginContactCallback_minion` (437083..437789) and no `ETHBeginContactCallback_ghost_minion`: the
  black knight gets none of its arms - the dark mage's `holdTime` cap (#12-55), `startEarthquake(0.8 x hitIntensity)` on
  an impact (#124-130) and `playFallSound(hitIntensity / 18)` above 3.5 (#132-140). And `ScoreDashboard`'s
  `spottedCount` (401234..401465 #5), `hasBeenUnnoticed` (401465..401641 #5) and `checkForLevelAchievements`'
  `countEntities` calls (#748-1165) read `'minion.ent'` alone. None of these is built on `main`: no minion impact
  tremble or fall sound, and `Achievements` decides medals only.
- **Where the aura is drawn.** An entity's particle piece is sorted at `particle->GetZPosition() + entity->GetPositionZ()
  + shift` (`ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:98-102`); `shift` is 0 for `ET_HORIZONTAL` (`type="0"`;
  `ETHEntityProperties.cpp:108-121`, `ETHParticleManager.cpp:332-335`); the start point is scaled with the system
  (`ETHParticleSystem.cpp:33`), so at `getScale()` it is -2 on the level's axis. The knight at 0.711 and its aura at
  **-1.289**: behind it. Particles live in world space, each released at its entity's position of that frame
  (`ETHParticleManager.cpp:507-523`).

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **`sim/Minions`** (R16): `Minion::entity` replaces `entityName` - the marker's `entityName`, or `Rules::defaultEntity`
  where it names none - and `Summon` gives an escort the same fallback. `Find` refuses a marker whose entity is not
  among `Rules::entities`, by the marker's and the entity's names. `minions.json` gains a `spawn` block, each number with
  its `_source`: `default_entity` `minion.ent`, `entities` [`minion.ent`, `ghost_minion.ent`] (and why one body serves
  both), `angle_deg` 0 and `scale` 1 (`spawnMinion` #25-39); `LoadRules` refuses a missing block, a fallback the list does
  not hold, and any scale but 1 (the body is stated at 1).
- **`MagicPortalsLayer`**: `EffectOwner::Kind::Minion` - a minion's entity point where its PICTURE is drawn this frame:
  the quad's transform (interpolated, in the app, between the last two ticks) back out through the pivot `syncMinions`
  placed it by; `EffectSpawn::picture` (false: the runtime draws no picture for an entity whose picture the layer draws
  itself) and `EffectSpawn::alwaysActive` (`ShouldEntityBeAlwaysActive`'s second arm, which the `.ent` reader cannot see;
  it decides only whether a hidden effect is stepped, and a minion owner is never hidden). `matchMinions` sets the black
  picture from the entity (the escort check falls away) and reads, once per entity, whether its `.ent` carries a
  particle system. `latchSimEffects` queues, once per such minion, its entity's systems: at its depth (`lookZ`), at
  `spawn.angle_deg` and `spawn.scale`, carried by it. `EffectReport` gains `followKind`, `followIndex` and `newbornPx`
  (where each particle the last step released was born), for the suite.
- **`sim/Effects`**: the blood row's z guard step 96 left for "the next step that relinks the simulation": `LoadRules`
  refuses a `blood` row whose z is not `{"value": 0, "scaled": true}` (its depth is the victim's own).
- **Data text**: `art.json` `minion.black_knight._source`, `ghost.json` `_not_built` and the `Ghost.hpp` comment no
  longer say the port spawns the default body.

**GAMEPLAY: none changes in play - which corrects the expectation this step was briefed with, that R16 changes 3-32.**
R16 is built - the sim holds `ghost_minion.ent` where the original does, and 12.2 reads it - but nothing the port plays
turns on it: the body is the one both files state (pinned on the files, 11 of 11 attributes and blocks equal); the
patrol, a killer floor, a key's carriers and a strike treat both entities alike in the original too; and what differs
by name - what the black knight adds when it dies (R4's), the contact callback's arms it never gets and the
`ScoreDashboard` counts that pass it by (above) - is not built on `main`. When one is built, the knight stays out of
it, as the original's does (track B's Q.2 already keeps it out of `minion_impact`: the backlog's merge note). MEASURED on 3-32's clip (below): the
player dies on tick 260 in both builds, and the band from the knight's feet to 5 u over them - below every aura
particle's dark disc (released at least 14.1 u over the feet, its dark part about 8.7 u in radius; only a turned quad's
near-white rim and corners reach lower) - is byte-identical on 60 of 61 frames over 39.8 u of patrol (the other, f306: 1 px,
8 levels in blue alone, at the band's top row). One new behaviour at load: a marker naming an entity `minions.json` does not list is refused; no level names
one (the census: 61 `minion.ent`, 1 `ghost_minion.ent`), and `test_mp_start` starts all 128 levels, 753 checks.

**THE DEPTH (K13): no new row.** The aura is the systems of an entity the script adds, so it takes the runtime's rule
for those as step 83 left it: `Slot::EffectSystems` in the slot `round(0.711 - 2) = -1` falls in. On level31b that is the
slot of its first z-0 picture (its five platforms carry no `z_index`): every picture at or below -1 is behind the aura

0), a placed portal (0) and the player (1.422) stand in later slots, in front of it - the original's order for every one
of them. `round` differs from the unrounded -1.289 only where a picture stands at exactly -1, which level31b has none of.
`TheBetweenSlotTableSaysWhereEachClassStands` is unchanged.

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.**
1. **CLOSED by the independent check: two gate rows rested on a suite that had not run.** Required: the unit case and

   checks, 0 failures), and both rows now pass on it (the table above), with deviation 5's caveat. `test_mp_diamonds`
   stays NOT RUN (refused twice); its only contact with this step is the renamed field.
2. **The aura follows the knight's drawn point, and the eyes do not follow the player's** (a finding, INFERRED from the
   code, not measured). `EffectOwner::Kind::Player` reads the sim body's tick point while the player's picture is drawn
   between ticks; under `--fixed-step` every frame is drawn at `Apply(0)`, the tick before, so the eyes would lead the
   drawn face by one tick's walk, up to 2.7 u at `player.json`'s 160 px/s. Not changed here (the effects runtime's, step
   84's eyes); filed in the backlog.
3. **Placed systems a few levels off where effect quads come and go.** The sweep: 23 px of 3-32's final door flame at
   f420, each in one channel only, by at most 9 levels (8 or 9 in red or blue, 5 in green). The gate clip
   (`work/steam_check.py`, `.json`): the gutter's steam differs on the frames it is in view (f60-f129, 54-172 px a
   frame), every channel within 9 levels, some by 1-3, where a steam particle moved by another random draw would
   differ by tens of levels over the dark wall. The clip's larger differences are effects on `m_effectRandom`: the red
   eyes (f57-f63, f123; 2-3 px on f153-f240) and, from the character's death on tick 260, its blood and smoke (up to 181
   levels). Attributed, INFERRED as step 96's deviation 9: effect quads made and pooled reshuffle the registry, so
   equal-depth quads sum in another order at the transparent sort's tie-break. The placement stream is untouched (K8).
4. **Not built: `startFrame` 4** (never drawn: the knight walks on its first update, `ETHCallback_minion` #1141-1162) and
   **`dragon_knight.ent`'s aura** (the same system; that knight exists only in 2-32's victory cutscene, which the port
   does not build).
5. **The new case reads the knight's report through a dangling pointer** (found by the independent check; recorded,
   not fixed). `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`, in `TheBlackKnightCarriesItsAuraAsAMultiply`, calls
   `MinionOf(layer.MinionReports(), "minion_spawn_908")` twice (the follow loop and the depth check), and
   `MinionReports()` returns its vector by value, so the pointer outlives the temporary; the older cases hold the vector
   first. The follow row's 0.000000 u is read through it (credible, undefined); **the depth check's comparison with the
   knight is vacuous**, and the knight z it prints is freed memory - not quoted here. The depth order stands, measured
   by the check from `out/levels/level31b.tscn` and the aura's printed z: the locked door -1.452, **the aura -1.4485**
   (slot 13: 13 pictures at `z_index` <= -1), the five z-0 platforms -1.448 to -1.432, the knight -1.430
   (`slotAfter(0.711)`, 18 pictures below it), the player -1.428 - the original's order. Why not fixed: a test edit
   relinks `test_mp_layer` and needs a launch under Smart App Control, and a commit changes text only. Owning follow-up:
   the next role that relinks the suite (the backlog row).

**R16** (step 97) is what it stands on: the sim knows which minion is the `ghost_minion.ent`. **R10** and **R12** are used,
not decided (the knight at the raw 2 over 2.8125). R1, R2, R22 and R23 are not built. **R24 and R25 (step 76) remain the
owner's to rule**; this step applies neither further.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (the listing `out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0`,
re-checked; the `.ent` files under `reference/extracted/assets/entities/`).
- **The spawn.** `ETHCallback_ghost_minion` (451487..451999): #1-6 `currentPos = GetPosition()`; #25 `ETHCallback_minion`,
  whose one `DeleteEntity` follows `isDestroyed` (#1478-1504) - a floor's `destroy`, a strike's, or its own burn
  (`isBurned` -> `destroy`, `addFlames`, #1456-1471); #35-40 `!IsAlive()`; #43-78 `AddEntity('ghost.ent', currentPos +
  vector3(0, 0, scale(-1)), 0, out, '', scale(0.3))`; #92-94 `playGhostAppearSound`; #96-103
  `DeleteEntity(SeekEntity(1430))`, level31b's `anti_sight_wall.ent`, a sensor with no sprite. A fireball burns a minion:
  `ETHBeginContactCallback_fireball` (418930..419710) #146-173 destroys itself and `burn()`s a non-sensor burnable, and
  `minion.ent` and `ghost_minion.ent` both carry `burnable 1`.
- **The init and the appearance.** `ETHCallback_ghost` (451999..457261) #26-324: hp 3, the red line, five `addWaypoint`
  calls (#173-301: the knight's point, the quarter point, ghost_pos three times; 1200 / 2500 / 50 / 0 / 0 ms;
  `FloatColor` 0xAA000000, 0xCC000000, 0xFFFFFFFF x 3; `defaultFilter` but the second leg's `smoothEnd`; scale
  `GetScale().x`, 0.6, 1, 1, 1), `ghost_appear_effect.ent` at `vector3(currentPos, GetPositionZ() + 1f)` (#150-169, a bare
  1) and `playGameMusic(true)` (#320-324). APPEARING (#369-494) plays them through `WaypointManager::update` (42421..42634,
  `FrameTimer::set` 23254..23650: at most one frame a call, the first call's reset) and `getCurrentPoint` (41513..42094),
  and on the fifth goes to SHOOTING with elapsedTime 3000.
- **The hover and the look.** SHOOTING (#499-512) and RAGE_MODE (#981-998) call `linearMotion(this, true, 0, PIb)` at the
  `.ent`'s speed 0.7 and stride 8; SHOOTING `SetFrame(0)`, RAGE_MODE `SetFrame(3)` and `SetAlpha(0.5)` and `SetAlpha(1)`
  on the way out (#1199-1201); DAMAGE `SetAlpha(0.5)` and `bounce(1 -> 1.1, 500)`; DEATH `SetAlpha(1)`, `bounce(1.1 ->
  1.25, 400)`, `StopSample` of the boss music (#1224-1243) and at 3550 ms `key.ent` at its own `GetPosition()`
  (#1354-1368). `bounce` (327057..327527) keeps one `blinkElapsedTime`, never reset.
- **The shot.** `addEnemyShoot` (434575..435266): `enemy_shoot.ent` at `vector3(casterPos, scale(10))`, `portal_mark.ent`
  at `vector3(finalPos, scale(32))`. `ETHCallback_enemy_shoot` (435266..436701): its first call moves it 16 units along
  `direction` and adds `projectile_shoot.ent` there (#1-71), its range measured from the muzzle; every call
  `SetFrame(_projectileFrameTimer.set(0, 5, 30, true))` and `SetAngle(getAngle(dir) - 90)` (#126-148); destroyed, it adds
  `portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent` at `vector3(its point, 0)` and `startEarthquake(10)` (#316-363).
- **The appear effect's own callback** (458062..458374): `followUp(this, ghost - scale(8, 8), 600, 100, true)` and
  `Scale(1.005f)` every frame - `followUp` (328407..329130) eases by `smoothEnd` over 600 ms and aims again after more
  than 100 ms while it has not arrived; `ETHEntity::Scale` grows every system's lengths and every live particle
  (`ETHEntity.cpp:591-599`, `ETHParticleManager.cpp:444-451`). D8 left `followUp`'s arguments undecoded; this step read
  them.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- **`sim/Ghost`**: `Spawn(knightPx)` - the ghost added at the dying knight's entity point, at the `.ent`'s own white and
  alpha 1 and scale 0.3, its init on the NEXT tick (INFERRED: `ghost.ent` is static, and a static entity's callback is
  queued from the draw pass, `ETHScene.cpp:547-572`); the init builds `Appear`, the WaypointManager as the listing plays it
  (`FrameTimer::set`'s reset, one frame a call, the current waypoint's filter, `min(stride, time) / max(stride, 1)`);
  `Look` (colour, alpha, scale, cell) written by each arm; the hover through `Motion::Linear` on the ghost's own point
  (`Alive()` now means added and not gone); every shot an id, its muzzle, its destiny, the 16-unit nudge, and
  `spentPx` for the layer; `keyName` for the key it drops. `ghost.json` gains `spawn`, `appear.waypoints`, `look`,
  `shot.cells`, and reads `shot.nudge_px`; `appear.total_ms` and the damage block's `alpha` go (the waypoints and `look`
  hold them).
- **`sim/Minions::Burn`** and `Death::byFire`; **`Game`**: the fireball block burns a minion it overlaps (after bombs,
  before the ghost); after the ghost's Tick, a death of `spawn.by_entity` adds the ghost and destroys node
  `anti_sight_wall_ent_1430`'s body (found by its id suffix, `tscn.py _node_name`).
- **`motions.json` `ghost`** (`Motion::Rules::ghost`): the one row whose motion the simulation keeps.
- **`MagicPortalsLayer`**: `Slot::Ghost` (after the escort's row, before the wall ghost's, -1/2); `syncGhost` on
  `hd/ghost.png` cut by `Tiers::FrameCut` (121 x 128 units), placed with its pivot on its point at its scale and tinted in
  `syncLighting` at the `Look`'s colour and alpha; `art.json` `ghost`. The effects runtime: a picture of more than one cell
  is cut by `FrameCut` with its uv written per frame (no longer the engine's even split), its pivot turned with its angle
  (`ComputeInScreenSpriteCenter`), an effect's own `followUp` and per-frame `Scale`, and three owners (`Ghost`,
  `GhostShot`, `Key`); `Effects::Spawn::zBaseUnits` for a bare literal over another entity's depth. `latchSimEffects`
  adds `ghost_appear_effect.ent` on the init tick, each shot's `enemy_shoot.ent`, `portal_mark.ent` and
  `projectile_shoot.ent`, a `portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent` where one ends, and the dropped key's `key.ent` with its bob
  (the key row, a start angle on `m_effectRandom`); `stepLevel` steps `_projectileFrameTimer` once per ghost shot after
  the player's (the order among callbacks INFERRED); `WantedTrack` (factored out of `updateMusic`) asks for the boss's
  music from the init and none from DEATH on.

1. **R4 on 3-32**: no ghost, no shot and no fire-diamond restock from the level's start until the black knight dies;
   the ghost then flies in from the knight's point over 3.75 s (SHOOTING on its 227th update, 226 after its init)
   instead of fading in at ghost_pos from the start. The knight can die by fire (below), by the killer floor, or by a
   strike.
2. **A fireball burns the minion it reaches**, on the four levels that place a fire diamond and minions (3-29 to 3-32,
   level28b-31b), the chapter-3 boss's escorts included - the original's `burnable 1`. An explosion's burn of a minion
   (level18b's bombs) is not built.

   the hovered point.
4. **A ghost shot starts 16 u out along its way** and its range is measured from the muzzle: it reaches the player's
   point 16 / 120 s (0.13 s) sooner.
5. Entity 1430's body is taken away with the knight; it is a sensor nothing in the port reads, so this changes nothing
   the port plays. Audio only: the boss's music from the ghost's init, silence from its DEATH.

## Step 100 - a scheduled tap is a press at that point: the controls read the tick's touch, and its pixels are the viewport's (built)

**TRACK B, and a step this run adds (T.1; not in 00_order section 7).** Built in the worktree
`Magic-Portals-Remake-vis4` (branch `visuals-d`, from `f1769ed`), whose build reads the frozen level data in
`out/snap_pre8`. Numbered from 120 up so that it cannot collide with track A's steps; the merge renumbers it. Game
only: `game/MagicPortalsLayer.{hpp,cpp}`, `game/main.cpp` (comment and `--help` text only) and
`tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`. No engine change, and the pin stays `4bfcf67`. No converter change and no data change.
**No gameplay change**: what a real press does is unchanged, and the argument and the measurements for that are
below. Spec: the backlog row "Found building step 80 (order 13.4): `--tap` cannot fire a portal shot, so no capture
can light a torch", and CLAUDE.md's rule that input goes through the port's one pointer path.

**THE ROW'S MECHANISM WAS ALREADY GONE WHEN THIS STEP BEGAN, and that is the first thing measured here.** The row was
written at `2bf4755` (2026-09-20 16:50), from step 80's tree. There `readInput` fired the shot from
`Input::MousePosition()`, and `helpBlockInput` returned before `touchThisTick` on a level with no help block. Step
87 (`5a60733`, the same day at 21:52, on the other track) had already changed `readInput`: it reads the tick's
`Touch` once, before `helpBlockInput`, and fires the shot from it (step 87's "The capture harness learns the tap it
always meant"). The merge `a5c9e23` carried that into `main`, and the row was never closed. On this tree's committed
build (`MagicPortals.exe` `3ad54ba2`, the binary that took the baseline sweep), before anything was changed:
`--level level28c --tap 247,141@60` logs `DEV tap down on tick 60 at (87.8222, 50.1333) units`, and then `the light
wall is going ... on tick 71`. Its f240 (`cab33202`) shows 4-29's torch lit, and the dashed ghost standing where the
wall was. **So gate 2 already held on the baseline. This step did not build it; this step keeps it.**

**WHAT WAS LEFT: two places where a scheduled tap and a real press still reached the shot by different roads.** Both
were measured on the same baseline build.
1. **The controls.** `readInput` asked `controlUnderPointer(registry)`, which read `Input` directly, and it skipped
   the question outright while any scheduled tap was due (`under = devTap ? nullptr : ...`). A real press on a HUD
   control is spent on the control. A scheduled tap at the same pixel went past the controls and fired a shot into
   the level under the button. Step 87's own record names this gap ("a scheduled `--tap` still cannot [press a
   control]"). Measured: `--level level3 --tap 1143,45@60` taps 1-04's restart button. It fired a shot into the
   top-right corner, the clear-portals button came up, and the level was loaded once (f120 `7cb7e456`).
2. **The tap's pixels.** `touchThisTick` put a scheduled tap's `atPx` at `at / view * (1280, 720)` whatever the
   window. The shot maps `atPx` as the VIEWPORT's pixels (`ViewportToLevelPx`), so in any window other than
   1280x720 the tap aimed somewhere else. `main.cpp` has always promised the opposite: "taps that pixel of a
   1280x720 window ... whatever the window's size". Measured: the 4-29 tap above in a 960x540 window opened a portal
   at (247, 141) of the 960x540 frame, a third further from the corner, and lit nothing (f240 `30ddcad3`).

**THE CHANGE.**
- `readInput` reads the tick's touch FIRST, after the back key's pause, and hands that one `Touch` to all three
  consumers: the controls, a help block and the shot. `controlUnderPointer` takes the `Touch` and tests
  `touch.atView`. The walk pads (held) and restart, pause and clear (edges) read `touch.held` and `touch.pressed`.
  The `devTap` flag is gone. The order is unchanged: controls first, then a help block, then the shot.
- `touchThisTick` puts a scheduled tap's `atPx` in the viewport's pixels, `at / view * viewport size`, and keeps
  1280x720 only where no viewport is published (where nothing can map it anyway).
- **For a REAL press nothing changes, expression for expression:**
  - `touch.over` is false in exactly the three cases where `controlUnderPointer` used to return early (no
    viewport, no `pointerOverGame`, or an empty viewport).
  - `touch.atView` is the same `glm::dvec2(local / size) * view` it computed, from the same `ViewPx()` and after the
    same `layOutControls()`.
  - Wherever `under` is not null, `touch.held` and `touch.pressed` ARE `Input::IsDown(kTap)` and
  `Input::TickWasPressed(kTap)`.
  - In a 1280x720 viewport a scheduled tap's `atPx` is also unchanged to the bit: `glm::dvec2(viewport->Size())` is
  exactly (1280.0, 720.0).
- **What changes for a capture, and it is the harness's alone:** a scheduled `--tap` on a HUD control now works the
  control, as a finger would, and no longer fires a shot beneath it. That is MEASURED for restart (gate 5 and
  `AScheduledTapOnAControlIsSpentOnIt`). Pause, clear and the walk pads take the same `touch.pressed` and
  `touch.held` in the same switch, so for them it follows from the code and was not captured. No capture script
  under `out/parity/` taps a control's rectangle during play:
  - 7.4's four taps are at (640, 360), (537, 308), (420, 330) and (620, 280);
  - the popup close that 1.1 and `ui2` use, at (1178, 358), is 376 px from the right pad's corner, against the
    pad's 180 px reach (`ui.json` `hud.pads.hit.radius_units` 64), and below restart and pause;
  - `ui3`'s taps land on the front door's menus, which `readInput` never reads.

  The captures below confirm all of this byte for byte. The pixels change reaches only the two readers of
  `touch.atPx`: the shot, and a help block's move length (`helpBlockInput`, against its 12 px). The menus, the
  credits and the dashboard read `touch.atView`, which did not change. Both readers change only off 1280x720, where
  they now measure what a real finger would. Of the 210 `--window` arguments in the capture scripts under
  `out/parity/`, 209 are 1280x720, and the one that is not is this step's own gate 2c.
- Comments: `ScheduleDevTap`, `Touch`, `controlUnderPointer`, and `main.cpp`'s `--tap` block and `--help` text now
  say where a scheduled tap goes during play. The pause's buttons and the end screens' buttons still read the mouse
  alone (`pauseTick`, `endScreenTick`); only the pause's buttons have `ScheduleDevPress`. They are not on the shot's
  path, and are left.

**THE DECODE, as built** (earthquake.json's `generator`, every number with its citation):
- One generator for the game, `g_earthquakeGen`. A call OVERWRITES its amplitude with
  `clamp(0.35 x intensity x s, 0, 50)` screen px and touches nothing else (`startEarthquake` 110309..110425).
- Each update that is due - 70 ms or more since the last tremble - trembles once: FORTH, the camera down by the
  amplitude, which is saved; or BACK, the camera up by the SAVED value, and only then the amplitude halves. Below
  1 px it stops, tested on every update. y only; no random source anywhere in the class (`update` 109902..110265;
  D11_check C8, C9). Built literally in `sim/Earthquake`, so a call between a forth and its back is halved before it
  is shown (F6's -5, +5, -10, +10 ...) and a sub-pixel call leaves the next shake opening on a back (C23) without
  any code of their own.
- **Where it applies**: after the camera's clamp and the portal manager's tap mapping, before the sky; the next
  frame's controller writes the camera whole again, so a tremble is a one-frame spike and nothing accumulates.

**THE CHANGE.**
- `sim/Earthquake` is the generator, renderer-free: `Start` and `Update` on a clock the caller keeps, `ToUnits` by
  the screen R12 takes, `InMouthLeg` for the dark dragon's re-armed row, and `LoadRules`, strict: every row and every
  number required.
- **The generator is tick state; the shake is frame state.** `OnFixedUpdate` is now `liftQuake`, the old body
  (`fixedTick`), then `quakeTick`, which lands the tick's calls on their two sides of one update on the layer's
  clock and keeps the move. `OnUpdate` adds that move to the camera the engine has just drawn between ticks
  (`shakeView`, after `InterpolationSystem::Apply`), and to every sky and satellite quad pinned to it. So a spike
  lasts one tick of time - the original's one frame at 60 fps - and the interpolation never smears it (D11 section
  3's hand-off 3). A frame draws the move of the LAST tick it ran: a frame that runs no tick draws the last move
  again, and a frame that runs two or more loses the moves of its earlier ticks, so below 60 fps some trembles are
  never drawn (deviation 1). The camera a TICK reads is never moved: the engine puts the tick's
  pose back at `BeginTick` and rewrites the drawn one at every `Apply`; outside the engine's loop (a suite calling
  `OnUpdate` 120 times in a row) `liftQuake` puts back the exact values it overwrote, so nothing drifts. `placeCamera`
  writes the camera whole and forgets the frame's move.
- **Taps stay at rest.** `ViewportToLevelPx` maps through the camera with the frame's move taken off, so every
  portal shot is aimed from the rest camera, as the original's portal manager aims it; the help blocks' rects are
  built from the rest follow and the controls from the viewport, as before.
- **The HUD does not move** (it is the screen overlay); the no-portal sign, which is a level entity in the original,
  moves with the world on a shaken frame (`EmitHud`).
- **Where it runs**: on every tick a level is shown - under the pause, a popup and the finished and lost screens
  (the original's clock is the wall clock and its controllers ignore the pause) - and not on a menu, where the
  generator waits. That a shake plays out under a pause follows from the code (`quakeTick` runs on the pause's
  ticks, and the layer clock advances on them); no capture pauses one.
- **The calls** (`latchSimQuakes` after `AfterStep`, beside `latchSimEffects`; `latchDoorQuakes` at the tick's end,
  because Puzzle moves its doors in `BeforeStep`). Each reads a counter or a flag the sims already keep, against the
  last tick's, and its first tick of a level only sets the mark, as the sound watch does. A call lands BEFORE the
  update when its caller runs before the generator in the original's frame (a begin-contact callback, a dynamic
  entity's callback) and AFTER it when it runs after (the game-state controller, a static entity's callback; each
  caller's `.ent` `static` read): earthquake.json `calls._when`.

- **Deviation 1 - a frame that runs two or more ticks draws only its last tick's shake move** (not a gate failure;
  no `--fixed-step` gate sees it). `quakeTick` overwrites `m_quakeOffsetUnits` every tick and `shakeView` reads it
  once per `OnUpdate`, and the engine runs up to 5 ticks in one frame (`engine/src/core/SupersonicApp.cpp:74`,
  `:1389`), so at a steady 30 fps every other tremble is never drawn in real play. Owning follow-up: this step's
  LEFT FOR LATER item - keep a nonzero move pending until one `OnUpdate` has drawn it, with a `test_mp_layer` case

- **Deviation 4 - the strip a shake uncovers shows the pinned sky where the original draws black bars** (not a gate

- **The unwired D11 rows** (not gate failures, recorded): rows 2, 6 and 14 wait on R23 / R15 and on 10.1; row 3 is
